newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols easier as spot drifts in ranges.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols easier as spot drifts in ranges.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were easier in U.S. trading as spot rates fluctuated in relatively narrow ranges after dollar/mark drifted off overnight highs, dealers said.

"There has been some aggressive selling in short-dated options, and the downward pressure is spilling over to one-month and out," said Masao Okada, chief options dealer at Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.
Although dollar/mark has been grinding higher each day, the move has been fairly orderly and long-anticipated, dealers said.
"There's no panic buying," said a European bank trader in Chicago. "There are people willing to sell into an up move."
One-month volatility for dollar/mark lost about 0.1 point from late Tuesday levels at 10.1/10.4 percent.

It had briefly risen to around 10.5 percent overnight when the dollar climbed to a fresh 34-month high of 1.7169 marks but soon pulled back along with spot, which was trading at just above 1.71 marks at U.S. midsession.
The dollar/mark volatility curve was still slightly inverted, with three-month at 10.0/10.2 percent and one-year at 9.85/9.95, but traders said it was gradually flattening.
Risk reversals, which reflect pricing differential between puts and calls, stayed well in favor of mark puts, reflecting widespread expectations of a higher dollar.
One-month 25-delta dollar/mark risk reversal was pegged at 0.3/0.6 percent skewed for mark puts.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen was down a quarter point from late Tuesday levels at 10.9/11.0 percent.
The dollar/yen curve was positively sloped in the front end due to time-decay pressure on the short-dateds but was virtually flat from three-month out to one-year at around 11.1/11.3 percent.
"It seems interbank dealers collectively have the highest gamma and vega exposures when the dollar is around mid-121 to mid-122 yen," Okada noted.
A high gamma position is vulnerable to a stagnant spot market, while a high vega position is vulnerable to declines in implied volatility levels.

But Okada warned that dealers tended to be short in low-delta strikes due to their sales to end-users and that volatilities could spike up once spot started moving toward recent boundaries of 120 and 125 yen.
He noted that low-delta options were becoming expensive relative to at-the-money ones.
Risk reversals were narrowly favoring yen calls in the front end. One-month 25-delta dollar/yen was at 0.0/0.4 percent skewed for yen calls.

The market was generally cautious ahead of the second leg of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony later in the day as well as employment data from Germany on Thursday and the U.S. on Friday. But traders said the slow grind in spot was taking its toll for now.
